Chapter 11 · Exhaustive Answer Keys & Step-by-Step Explanations

This chapter gathers the complete answer key for every exercise in Chapters 1 to 10 into one place, so you can check your work without flicking between chapters. Each answer gives the correct form, a short reason in clear English, and, where the error is one that Bangla speakers make often, a supporting Bangla (BN) note explaining why the correct answer works and why the common mistake fails. Use it honestly: attempt every exercise with a pen first, then check here. The reason matters more than the answer. If you got an item wrong, note its error code (SVA, T, A, P, WF, C, WW, COND) and add it to your personal audit list from Chapter 10. Two or three codes usually account for most of your lost marks; drill those. অধ্যায় ১১-এর মূল কথা: এখানে অধ্যায় ১ থেকে ১০-এর প্রতিটি অনুশীলনের সম্পূর্ণ উত্তর এক জায়গায় আছে, প্রতিটির সঙ্গে সংক্ষিপ্ত কারণ (ইংরেজিতে) ও দরকারে বাংলা টীকা। আগে কলম দিয়ে চেষ্টা করুন, তারপর মিলিয়ে দেখুন; ভু ল হলে তার error code টু কে রাখুন।
Chapter 1 · Subject-Verb Agreement & Sentence Foundations
Exercise 1.1 · Identification and Correction

1. The list of approved candidates is posted on the noticeboard. Subject is “list” (singular),  not “candidates.” BN: subject “list”, মাঝের “of candidates” বাদ দিলে বোঝা যায়।  2. Each of the students has submitted his or her assignment. “Each of” is always singular.  BN: each of সবসময় singular, তাই has।

3. The government is introducing a new tax next year. Collective noun as one unit takes a  singular verb in academic writing.  4. Neither the teacher nor the students were ready for the test. With “neither…nor,” the  verb agrees with the nearer subject, “students” (plural).  5. The number of accidents on this road has increased. “The number of” is singular. BN:  “the number of” সবসময় singular।  6. There are several reasons for this decline. The real subject “reasons” is plural.  7. A large amount of information was collected during the survey. “Information” is  uncountable and singular, so “amount … was.” BN: information uncountable, singular।  8. Ten kilometres is a long way to walk in the heat. A single distance is treated as one  quantity: singular verb.  9. Correct. “Committee” as one unit takes the singular “has.”  10. The quality of the roads in rural areas is very poor. Subject is “quality” (singular), not  “roads” or “areas.”  11. Poverty and illiteracy remain major obstacles to development. Two subjects joined by  “and” are plural.  12. Everyone in the two classes was given a certificate. “Everyone” is singular. BN: everyone  singular, তাই was।  13. Not only the manager but also the workers are unhappy with the plan. With “not only…  but also,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “workers” (plural).  14. Correct. “Data” is treated as a plural or mass noun; “the data … show” is acceptable and  consistent here.  15. My knowledge of these topics is limited. “Knowledge” is uncountable and singular;  subject is “knowledge,” not “topics.”  16. A number of students have failed to register on time. “A number of” means “several” and  takes a plural verb.  17. The population of the coastal cities has grown rapidly. Subject is “population” (singular),  not “cities.”  18. Neither of the two proposals seems practical. “Neither” is singular. BN: neither singular,  তাই seems।  19. Correct. “Statistics” as the name of a subject is singular: “statistics is.”  20. The equipment in the laboratories needs to be replaced. “Equipment” is uncountable  and singular. BN: equipment uncountable, singular। Note: questions 9, 14 and 19 are the correct ones. The instruction
said two were correct; number 14 is the deliberate extra, included so you cannot simply assume “exactly two.” Real proofreading means checking every sentence, not counting to a target.
Exercise 1.2 · IELTS Essay Editing

The ten errors are corrected in bold below.  Nowadays, the number of people who work from home has increased dramatically.  There are many reasons for this change. First, technology allows employees to stay  connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offers flexible

arrangements. However, some managers believe that productivity falls when staff  are not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweigh the  disadvantages, and this trend is likely to continue. The ten corrections, with reasons:  1. who works → who work: “who” refers to “people” (plural).  2. have increased → has increased: the subject is “the number” (singular).  3. There is many reasons → There are many reasons: the real subject “reasons” is plural.  4. technology allow → technology allows: “technology” is singular third person.  5. each of the major companies now offer → offers: “each of” is singular.  6. some managers believes → believe: “managers” is plural.  7. productivity fall → falls: “productivity” is singular (and uncountable).  8. staff is not → staff are not: here the focus is on the individual workers; plural reads  better, and “are” is safe. (Singular “the staff is” is also defensible, but the following idea  is about individual people not being present.)  9. the advantages … outweighs → outweigh: the subject is “advantages” (plural), not  “work.”  10. this trend are → this trend is: “trend” is singular. BN: এই অনুচ্ছেদে দশটি ভু লই subject খুঁজে বের করে verb মেলানোর অভাবে হয়েছে। মূল কৌশল: subject আর verb-এর মাঝের সব শব্দ বাদ দিয়ে subject-টি বের করা, তারপর singular না plural সেই অনুযায়ী verb বসানো।
Chapter 2 · Tense Mastery & Time Precision
Exercise 2.1 · Tense Selection

1. opened: finished year (2008), past simple.  2. has invested: “since 2015” reaches to now, present perfect.  3. is rising: “at the moment”, present continuous. BN: at the moment মানে এখন চলছে।  4. freezes: general scientific truth, present simple.  5. had already changed: an action completed before another past event, past perfect.  6. know: “I am knowing” is wrong; know is stative and stays simple present. BN: stative  verb, continuous হয় না।  7. have been increasing (or have increased): “for the last ten years” reaches to now;  present perfect continuous stresses the duration.  8. will double: a real future prediction, first-conditional future with “will.”  9. rose: “last summer” is finished time, past simple.  10. are working: “nowadays” plus a current trend, present continuous.  11. closed: a finished event (1998), past simple. (The second clause correctly uses present  perfect “has never reopened.”)  12. has transformed: “over the past decade” reaches to now, present perfect.

13. has: possession is stative; “is having” would be wrong here. BN: মালিকানা বোঝাতে have,  continuous নয়।  14. fell: a finished past range (2000 to 2010), past simple.  15. is considering: “currently”, present continuous.  16. understands: “is understanding” is wrong; understand is stative, present simple. BN:  stative verb।  17. will be: a future prediction for a future point, future simple.  18. dropped: tied to a finished year (2012), past simple.  19. have grown: “so far this year” reaches to now, present perfect.  20. spend: a repeated general truth (“every year”), present simple.
Exercise 2.2 · Task 1 Trend Description (model answer)

In 1990, coffee consumption in Country X was low, at roughly 2 kilograms per person.  It then rose steadily throughout the 1990s, reaching 5 kilograms by 2000.  Consumption fell slightly between 2005 and 2010, but it has risen every year since,  and it now stands at about 8 kilograms per person. Looking ahead, the figure is  projected to reach 10 kilograms by 2030. Why the tenses are what they are:  • was, rose, reaching, fell: all finished past data with stated years, so past simple (plus  one present participle “reaching” to link the result smoothly).  • has risen: “every year since 2010, up to now”, present perfect, because the change  reaches the present.  • now stands: the present situation in 2025, present simple.  • is projected to reach: a future forecast, a future form (here the passive “is projected to,”  which is more academic than a bare “will”). BN: এই অনুচ্ছেদে তিনটি সময় আলাদা tense-এ আছে: শেষ হওয়া ডেটা past simple, ২০১০ থেকে এখন পর্যন্ত পরিবর্তন present perfect, আর ভবিষ্যতের পূর্বাভাস future form (“is projected to”). একই অনুচ্ছেদে সময় বদলালে tense- ও বদলাবে, এটাই Task 1-এর মূল দক্ষতা।
Chapter 3 · Articles & Noun Types
Exercise 3.1 · Article Insertion

1. (0) Education is the key to (0) economic development. Why: general uncountable  “education” and “development” take zero article; “the key” is specific.  2. She is the most hard-working student in the class. Superlative and a specific class both  take “the.”  3. The chart shows the number of tourists visiting a museum. “the chart,” “the number  of,” first-mention “a museum.”

4. The internet has transformed the way people communicate. “the internet” is unique;  “the way” is specified by the clause after it. 5. He wants to become an honest lawyer after (0) university. “an” before the vowel sound  of “honest” (silent h); “university” as an institution takes zero article. BN: honest-এর h  উচ্চারিত হয় না, তাই an। 6. (0) Pollution is a serious problem in (0) major cities. General uncountable “pollution”;  “a problem” first mention; general plural “cities.” 7. I read an interesting article yesterday. The article was about (0) climate change. First  mention “an,” second mention “the,” general “climate change.” 8. The government should invest more in (0) public transport. “the government” is  specific; “public transport” is a general uncountable. 9. The United States and the United Kingdom signed an agreement. These country names  take “the”; “an agreement” first mention. BN: the United States, the United Kingdom  সবসময় the নেয়। 10. The sun rises in the east. Both unique. 11. (0) Poverty remains an obstacle to (0) progress in the developing world. General  “poverty” and “progress”; “an obstacle” first mention; “the developing world” is specific. 12. She gave me (0) useful advice about the visa process. “advice” is uncountable (no “a”);  “the visa process” is specific. BN: advice uncountable, তাই a বসে না। 13. The number of (0) students who fail the exam is rising. “the number of,” general  “students,” the specific “exam.” 14. My brother is an engineer, and he works for a large company. “an engineer” (vowel  sound), “a company” first mention. 15. (0) Water is essential for (0) life on (0) Earth. General uncountables and the proper  noun “Earth” take zero article. 16. We stayed in a hotel near the airport; the hotel was cheap. First mention “a hotel,” the  known “the airport,” second mention “the hotel.” 17. (0) Research shows that (0) exercise improves (0) mental health. All  general/uncountable, zero article. BN: research uncountable। 18. The environment must be protected for (0) future generations. “the environment” is  unique; “future generations” general plural. 19. He spent an hour reading a book about the history of (0) Bangladesh.

“an hour” (silent  h), “a book” first mention, “the history of X” specific, proper noun “Bangladesh” zero. 20. The traffic in the capital is a major source of (0) air pollution. “the traffic” specific, “the  capital” specific, “a source” first mention, general “air pollution.” 21. (0) Knowledge is power, but (0) information alone is not (0) knowledge. All general  uncountables. 22. She is the best doctor in the hospital where I work. Superlative and a specified hospital. 23. (0) Children in (0) rural areas often lack access to (0) good schools. General plurals  throughout. 24. The economy grew by (0) five per cent in the first quarter. “the economy” unique, “five  per cent” no article, “the first quarter” ordinal. 25. (0) Solar power is a cleaner alternative to (0) fossil fuels. General uncountable “solar  power,” “a cleaner alternative” first mention, general plural “fossil fuels.”
Exercise 3.2 · Countable versus Uncountable Error Spotting

1. The teacher gave us much useful advice before the exam. (“advice” is uncountable: no  plural, use “much” not “many.”) BN: advice এর plural হয় না।  2. I need some information about the application process. (“information” is  uncountable.)  3. She bought new furniture for her apartment. (“furniture” has no plural; use “pieces of  furniture” if counting.)  4. The laboratory does not have enough equipment. (“equipment” is uncountable.)  5. He has made good progress in his studies this year. (“progress” is uncountable: no “a.”)  6. The researchers published several important studies last year. (“research” is  uncountable; the countable word is “studies.”) BN: research uncountable, গুনতে হলে  studies।  7. We had a lot of homework during the holidays. (“homework” is uncountable.)  8. The company installed new software on every computer. (“software” is uncountable.)  9. There was heavy traffic on the road this morning. (“traffic” is uncountable: no plural,  and “was,” not “were.”)  10. The hotel provides free accommodation for its staff. (both uncountable: no plural.)  11. My knowledge of physics is quite limited. (“knowledge” is uncountable and singular.)  12. The government spent a huge amount of money on the project. (“money” is  uncountable: no “a” directly.)  13. She gave me two pieces of good news / some good news yesterday. (“news” is  uncountable despite the final -s.) BN: news শেষে -s থাকলেও uncountable।  14. The students carried heavy luggage to the airport. (“luggage” is uncountable; count  with “pieces of luggage.”)  15. The report contains much useful data about the economy. (“data” is treated as  uncountable/mass here; “datas” is never correct.) BN: এই দুটো অনুশীলনের মূল শিক্ষা: প্রথমে ঠিক করুন noun-টি countable না uncountable; uncountable হলে কখনো plural -s বা a/an বসবে না, আর গুনতে হলে a piece of / an item of / an amount of ব্যবহার করুন। এরপর article-এর চারটি প্রশ্ন ধাপে ধাপে খাটান।
Chapter 4 · Prepositions & Dependency Rules
Exercise 4.1 · Preposition Fill-in

1. by: the size of a change.  2. from … to … in: start, end, and the year.  3. from: “result from” a cause.  4. in: “invest in.”  5. in: “interested in” (+ the -ing form “studying”).  6. to: “lead to.”  7. at … in: peak “at” a value, “in” a year.

8. on: “depend on.”  9. from … of: “suffer from” a “lack of.”  10. for: “responsible for” (+ -ing “managing”).  11. to: “related to.”  12. (0): “discuss” takes a direct object, no preposition. BN: discuss about ভু ল।  13. in … for: an “increase in,” a “demand for.”  14. of: “consist of.”  15. on … at: “on Fridays,” “at the weekend.”  16. to … of: “fell to a low of.”  17. on: “rely on.”  18. on … of: “focus on,” “effects of.”  19. (0): “enter” takes a direct object. BN: enter into ভু ল।  20. to: “similar to.”  21. from: “benefit from.”  22. for … to: “apply for” a scholarship, “to” an institution.  23. to: “solution to.”  24. since: “since 2000” (a starting point, with the present perfect).  25. to: “according to the chart” (a source, which is correct here).
Exercise 4.2 · L1 Direct-Translation Fix

1. In my opinion, the government should act quickly. (“according to me” is wrong for your  own view.) BN: “আমার মতে” = in my opinion।  2. We discussed the new policy for an hour. (“discuss” needs no “about.”)  3. He entered the classroom without knocking. (“enter” needs no “into.”)  4. The teacher emphasised the importance of grammar. (or “placed emphasis on”;  “emphasise” takes a direct object.) BN: emphasise on ভু ল।  5. After the trip, they returned to their village. (“return” already means “go back,” so  “back” is redundant.)  6. The report comprises five main sections. (or “is composed of”; “comprise” takes no “of.”)  7. She married a doctor last year. (“marry” takes a direct object.)  8. I want to ask you for some help / make a request to you for some help. (“request to  you” is wrong.)  9. The essay mentioned three possible solutions. (“mention” needs no “about.”)  10. The researchers investigated the causes of pollution. (“investigate” takes a direct  object.)  11. We must cope with the rising cost of living. (no “up.”) BN: cope up with ভু ল, সঠিক cope  with।  12. The minister reached the venue an hour late. (“reach” takes no “to.”)  13. My opinion is different from yours on this matter. (“different from” is the standard  academic form.)  14. Students should concentrate on their studies. (“concentrate on,” not “in.”)  15. The country is suffering from severe traffic congestion. (“suffer from.”)

এই অধ্যায়ের মূল কৌশল: (১) data preposition (by, from…to, of, at) fixed phrase হিসেবে মুখস্থ; (২)
dependent preposition (depend on, lead to, responsible for) block আকারে মুখস্থ; (৩) সরাসরি অনুবাদ বন্ধ
করুন, কারণ discuss about, according to me, enter into, return back সব বাংলা প্রভাবজনিত ভু ল।

blocks.text: Chapter 5 · Complex Sentences & Subordinate Clauses
Exercise 5.1 · Sentence Combining (model answers)

1. Although public transport is cheap, many people still drive.  2. The lake dried up because rainfall had declined for years.  3. The company hired a manager who had ten years of experience.  4. Governments that invest in education tend to see their economies grow faster.  5. Once fees rose sharply, enrolment dropped. (or “When fees rose …”)  6. The city built new cycle lanes in order to cut congestion.  7. Although renewable energy is expensive at first, it becomes cheaper over time.  8. The report, which was published last year, highlighted the housing crisis. (non-  defining: commas.)  9. Unless action is taken soon, the situation will worsen.  10. Many families who live in rural areas lack access to good hospitals.  11. Although the policy was popular, it was eventually withdrawn.  12. Solar power, which is clean, is expanding rapidly. (non-defining: commas.)  13. Prices rose sharply because demand outstripped supply.  14. Students who study abroad gain independence and confidence.  15. When the factory closed in 1998, hundreds of workers lost their jobs.  16. Because cities are crowded and expensive, young workers often leave them.  17. The government raises taxes so that public services can be funded properly.  18. This is the town where I grew up.  19. Even though technology keeps advancing, many traditional jobs are  disappearing. (concession.)  20. While some countries recycle most of their waste, others send it to landfill.
Exercise 5.2 · Punctuation and Relative-Clause Polish

1. The city that is famous for its food attracts many tourists. (Defining clause: no  commas. “which” also acceptable.)  2. My brother, who lives in Canada, is an engineer. (Only one brother, so the clause is  non-defining: commas.) BN: একটাই ভাই, তাই non-defining, কমা দিন।  3. Students who cheat in exams are usually expelled. (Remove the repeated subject  “they.”) BN: relative clause-এর পরে আবার they বসবে না।  4. The report was clear; it recommended three changes. (Fix the comma splice with a  semicolon or full stop.)

5. Although the policy was expensive, it reduced accidents significantly. (Join the  fragment to the main clause with a comma.)  6. Solar power, which is renewable, is becoming cheaper. (Non-defining: commas on  both sides.)  7. People who live near factories often suffer from poor air quality. (“who” for  people, not “which.”) BN: মানুষের জন্য who, which নয়।  8. Governments that invest in transport tend to see lower long-term costs.  (Defining clause: remove the stray comma.)  9. The scheme was popular; however, it was cancelled after two years. (“however”  cannot join two clauses with only a comma; use a semicolon.)  10. Correct. (“whose” for possession, non-defining reading with the class specified; the  sentence is already well formed.)  11. Because the weather was extremely bad, the outdoor event was postponed. (Join  the fragment.)  12. Dhaka, which is the capital of Bangladesh, is extremely crowded. (Non-defining: a  unique place, so commas.)  13. The students were tired, so they left the lecture early. (Fix the comma splice / run-  on with “so.”)  14. This is the hospital where my mother works. (Remove the repeated subject “she.”)  15. The company hired a candidate whose qualifications were outstanding.  (Possession needs “whose,” not “that.”) BN: মালিকানা বোঝাতে whose। BN: এই অধ্যায়ের মূল কৌশল: (১) fronted dependent clause-এর পরে কমা; (২) defining clause-এ কমা নেই, non-defining-এ দুই পাশে কমা; (৩) that শুধু defining-এ; (৪) relative clause-এর পরে subject আবার (they/it/she) বসাবেন না; (৫) দুই independent clause শুধু কমা দিয়ে জোড়া যায় না।
Chapter 6 · Passive Voice & Academic Detachment
Exercise 6.1 · Active to Passive Transformation

1. The crop is harvested (by farmers) in October. (present simple.)  2. A new bridge will be built next year. (future.)  3. The report was written by the committee. (past simple; participle “written.”) BN: write-  এর participle written।  4. The road is being repaired at the moment. (present continuous.)  5. A great deal of water has been wasted. (present perfect.)  6. New laws were introduced in 2019. (past simple.)  7. The equipment must be cleaned after every use. (modal.)  8. The raw materials are processed (by machines). (present simple.)  9. The survey had been completed before the deadline. (past perfect.)  10. Thousands of trees are being planted this year. (present continuous.)  11. Two thousand cars are produced a day. (present simple.)

12. The building was designed by a famous architect. (the “by” phrase adds real  information, so keep it.)  13. Recycling should be encouraged (by the authorities). (modal.)  14. The new system is being tested. (present continuous.)  15. It is believed that tourism damages the environment. (impersonal passive.) BN: নৈর্ব্যক্তিক  গঠন।
Exercise 6.2 · Process Diagram Writing (model answer, about 150 words)

The diagram illustrates the process by which used glass bottles are recycled into  new ones. First, used bottles are collected from homes and public bins, after which  they are transported to a recycling plant. On arrival, the glass is sorted by colour  into clear, green, and brown, and it is then washed thoroughly so that labels and dirt  are removed. Next, the clean glass is crushed into small fragments known as cullet.  Once this stage is complete, the cullet is melted in a furnace at an extremely high  temperature until it becomes liquid. The molten glass is then moulded into the  shape of new bottles. Finally, the finished bottles are filled, labelled, and sent to  shops, where the cycle can begin again. Throughout the process, each stage is carried  out in a fixed sequence, with the output of one step becoming the input of the next.  (150 words) Why it works: every step is in the passive present simple (are collected, is sorted, is melted, are sent), because the doer is irrelevant; the sequence is held together by ordering words (first, then, next, once, finally); and the tense stays consistent from start to finish. BN: পুরো বর্ণনাটি passive present simple-এ (are collected, is washed, is melted), কারণ কে করছে তা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ নয়; ধাপগুলো first, then, next, once, finally দিয়ে সাজানো; এবং tense শুরু থেকে শেষ পর্যন্ত একই থাকে। এটাই Task 1 process-এর আদর্শ কাঠামো।

exercises.title: Exercise 1.1 · Identification and Correction
exercises.instructions: Each sentence below contains a subject-verb agreement error, except a few which are already correct. Rewrite each faulty sentence correctly, and for the correct ones write "Correct."

items.prompt: The list of approved candidates are posted on the noticeboard.
items.answer: The list of approved candidates is posted on the noticeboard.
accepted: The list of approved candidates is posted on the noticeboard.
items.reason: Subject is "list" (singular), not "candidates."
items.bn_note: subject "list", মাঝের "of candidates" বাদ দিলে বোঝা যায়।

items.prompt: Each of the students have submitted their assignment.
items.answer: Each of the students has submitted his or her assignment.
accepted: Each of the students has submitted their assignment.
Each of the students has submitted his or her assignment.
items.reason: "Each of" is always singular.
items.bn_note: each of সবসময় singular, তাই has।

items.prompt: The government are introducing a new tax next year.
items.answer: The government is introducing a new tax next year.
accepted: The government is introducing a new tax next year.
items.reason: Collective noun as one unit takes a singular verb in academic writing.

items.prompt: Neither the teacher nor the students was ready for the test.
items.answer: Neither the teacher nor the students were ready for the test.
accepted: Neither the teacher nor the students were ready for the test.
items.reason: With "neither…nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "students" (plural).

items.prompt: The number of accidents on this road have increased.
items.answer: The number of accidents on this road has increased.
accepted: The number of accidents on this road has increased.
items.reason: "The number of" is singular.

items.prompt: There is several reasons for this decline.
items.answer: There are several reasons for this decline.
accepted: There are several reasons for this decline.
items.reason: The real subject "reasons" is plural.

items.prompt: A large amount of information were collected during the survey.
items.answer: A large amount of information was collected during the survey.
accepted: A large amount of information was collected during the survey.
items.reason: "Information" is uncountable and singular.

items.prompt: Ten kilometres are a long way to walk in the heat.
items.answer: Ten kilometres is a long way to walk in the heat.
accepted: Ten kilometres is a long way to walk in the heat.
Ten kilometers is a long way to walk in the heat.
items.reason: A single distance is treated as one quantity: singular verb.

items.prompt: The committee has agreed on the final budget.
items.answer: Correct
accepted: Correct
correct
The committee has agreed on the final budget.
items.reason: "Committee" as one unit takes the singular "has."

items.prompt: The quality of the roads in rural areas are very poor.
items.answer: The quality of the roads in rural areas is very poor.
accepted: The quality of the roads in rural areas is very poor.
items.reason: Subject is "quality" (singular), not "roads" or "areas."

items.prompt: Poverty and illiteracy remains major obstacles to development.
items.answer: Poverty and illiteracy remain major obstacles to development.
accepted: Poverty and illiteracy remain major obstacles to development.
items.reason: Two subjects joined by "and" are plural.

items.prompt: Everyone in the two classes were given a certificate.
items.answer: Everyone in the two classes was given a certificate.
accepted: Everyone in the two classes was given a certificate.
items.reason: "Everyone" is singular.

items.prompt: Not only the manager but also the workers is unhappy with the plan.
items.answer: Not only the manager but also the workers are unhappy with the plan.
accepted: Not only the manager but also the workers are unhappy with the plan.
items.reason: With "not only…but also," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "workers" (plural).

items.prompt: The data collected over ten years show a clear pattern.
items.answer: Correct
accepted: Correct
correct
The data collected over ten years show a clear pattern.
The data collected over ten years shows a clear pattern.
items.reason: "Data" is treated as a plural or mass noun; "the data … show" is acceptable.

items.prompt: My knowledge of these topics are limited.
items.answer: My knowledge of these topics is limited.
accepted: My knowledge of these topics is limited.
items.reason: "Knowledge" is uncountable and singular; subject is "knowledge," not "topics."

items.prompt: A number of students has failed to register on time.
items.answer: A number of students have failed to register on time.
accepted: A number of students have failed to register on time.
items.reason: "A number of" means "several" and takes a plural verb.

items.prompt: The population of the coastal cities have grown rapidly.
items.answer: The population of the coastal cities has grown rapidly.
accepted: The population of the coastal cities has grown rapidly.
items.reason: Subject is "population" (singular), not "cities."

items.prompt: Neither of the two proposals seem practical.
items.answer: Neither of the two proposals seems practical.
accepted: Neither of the two proposals seems practical.
items.reason: "Neither" is singular.

items.prompt: Statistics is a subject that many students find difficult.
items.answer: Correct
accepted: Correct
correct
Statistics is a subject that many students find difficult.
items.reason: "Statistics" as the name of a subject is singular.

items.prompt: The equipment in the laboratories need to be replaced.
items.answer: The equipment in the laboratories needs to be replaced.
accepted: The equipment in the laboratories needs to be replaced.
items.reason: "Equipment" is uncountable and singular.

exercises.title: Exercise 1.2 · IELTS Essay Editing
exercises.instructions: The paragraph below is from a Band 5.5 Task 2 essay. It contains ten subject-verb agreement errors. Find them, then rewrite the whole paragraph correctly.

items.prompt: Nowadays, the number of people who works from home have increased dramatically. There is many reasons for this change. First, technology allow employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offer flexible arrangements. However, some managers believes that productivity fall when staff is not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweighs the disadvantages, and this trend are likely to continue.
items.answer: Nowadays, the number of people who work from home has increased dramatically. There are many reasons for this change. First, technology allows employees to stay connected from anywhere. Second, each of the major companies now offers flexible arrangements. However, some managers believe that productivity falls when staff are not in the office. In my opinion, the advantages of remote work outweigh the disadvantages, and this trend is likely to continue.
items.reason: Ten corrections: who work; has increased; There are; technology allows; offers; believe; falls; staff are; outweigh; this trend is.
items.bn_note: এই অনুচ্ছেদে দশটি ভুলই subject খুঁজে বের করে verb মেলানোর অভাবে হয়েছে। মূল কৌশল: subject আর verb-এর মাঝের সব শব্দ বাদ দিয়ে subject-টি বের করা।
